Ridu 0.2.3 removes the legacy `JWT` authorization-header alias for opaque session tokens.

## Authentication

HTTP and GraphQL clients authenticate sessions with `Authorization: Session <token>` or the HttpOnly `ridu_session` cookie. API keys continue to use `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The authentication guides and generated project reference now describe these three credential forms.

## Breaking change and upgrading

Replace `Authorization: JWT <token>` with `Authorization: Session <token>`. The existing opaque session token can be reused; this change does not revoke sessions or require users to sign in again. The `JWT` scheme no longer authenticates a session or supplies a token to GraphQL session-refresh operations.

Upgrade the Go module, project-local CLI, framework npm packages and official plugins together to **0.2.3**, then regenerate application contracts and run application checks.

Go configuration, generated contract shapes, HTTP routes, SDK signatures and plugin provider signatures are unchanged. Backend and admin API markers remain **1**; admin authoring, pairing, manifest, protocol and migration/planner versions are unchanged.

No database migration, authentication-state conversion or maintenance window is required for this change. Historical migration artifacts and ordinary collection-backed persistence are unchanged.
